prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Conroe, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1274; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you were involved in on a roadway in Conroe, Texas. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just go by my initials for this, if that's okay.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me, in your own words, what happened?

A: I was driving along a two-lane road, going maybe thirty miles an hour. A car coming the other way drifted into my lane. I braked and turned a little, but we still hit front to front. It wasn't a big impact, but it was enough to jolt me.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt at the time?

A: Yes, I was buckled in.

Q: Did your airbags deploy?

A: No, they didn't. My car just stopped pretty hard, and my head snapped forward and then back.

Q: Did you get out of the vehicle at the scene, or did you stay inside?

A: I got out after a minute. I felt a little dizzy and my neck was already stiff.

Q: Have you sought medical attention since the collision?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic that same afternoon. They said I had whiplash and gave me a neck brace and some pain medication.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Yes. My neck is sore when I turn my head, and I get headaches most evenings. I've had to take time off from my physical therapy job because lifting hurts.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything you'd like to add?

A: Just that I want my car repaired and my medical bills looked at. I've been cooperating and I want this handled fairly.

Q: Thank you for your time. This concludes the statement.
